title: NCLT Kolkata: Bank Records Can Prove a Loan Even Without a Written Agreement
case_name: Piyush Securities Private Limited v. Shree Vaishnavi Ispat Limited
citation: Section 7 petition, NCLT Kolkata Bench-II, order reported 29 October 2026
card_summary: The Kolkata bench of the NCLT admitted a Section 7 petition by non-banking lender Piyush Securities against Shree Vaishnavi Ispat over a default of about Rs 5.52 crore. The debtor argued no written loan agreement existed, but the tribunal held an oral inter-corporate loan corroborated by bank records and the debtor's own balance sheet proved the debt. The company now enters insolvency resolution.
card_tip: Group companies that lend to each other without signing a loan deed should still keep bank transfer records and written acknowledgments; those alone can support a financial creditor's claim before the NCLT.
verification_notes: Confirmed via two independent reports (Taxscan, TaxGuru) of the same NCLT Kolkata Bench-II order and holding. Exact order date not independently located; 29 October 2026 is the date both outlets reported the ruling, and the order itself falls within the scope window.
